question: Why can a cause never exist without its effect?
premises: A cause never exists anywhere without its own effect.
Causality is the fitness of that cause.
That fitness is conditioned by the immediacy of the fruit.
inference: Cause and effect are bound so tightly that causality means a fitness resting on the fruit's immediacy.
uncertainties: phalānantaryabhāvitā read as 'conditioned by the immediacy of fruit'; an alternative parse 'existing in the fruit's non-immediacy' is not excluded.
plain_english: A cause never exists at any time without its own effect; this fitness is causality itself, conditioned by the immediacy of the fruit.
